CyUI / Documentation

Build on a common foundation.

A practical guide to selecting modules, embedding CyUI and keeping the host application in charge. This HTML guide is available in English and French and opens offline.

The detailed API references currently live in the repository in English. Links to those references are explicitly marked; they require a connection and repository access.

1. Start with Core

CyUI compiles against the host application’s Dear ImGui instance. Requirements: Dear ImGui ≥ 1.92, CMake ≥ 3.16 and C++17 for Core. CodeEditor and the tested CEF adapter require C++20. The docking branch is recommended when your application uses docking.

Place the repository in external/CyUI and name the existing ImGui target with CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET. Disable unused Audio and Gallery options: their original defaults are ON. Select only the optional families you need.

CMakeLists.txt
set(CYUI_IMGUI_TARGET app_imgui)
set(CYUI_BUILD_DEMO OFF)
set(CYUI_BUILD_AUDIO OFF)
set(CYUI_BUILD_GALLERY OFF)
set(CYUI_MODULES "Nodes;Inspector")
add_subdirectory(external/CyUI)

target_link_libraries(app PRIVATE
    CyUI::Nodes CyUI::Inspector)

Initialize once, draw each frame

After creating each ImGui context, apply the CyUI configuration and load suitable system or host-supplied fonts. Keep the application’s normal NewFrame/Render lifecycle.

C++
#include <cyui/Core.h>

// Once, after ImGui::CreateContext():
cyui::Config config;
config.themeKey = "mid-grey";
cyui::apply(config);
cyui::loadFonts();

// During an ImGui frame:
if (cyui::primaryButton(cyui::trLabel("Save").c_str())) {
    saveDocument();
}
cyui::renderNotifications();

Use palette() color roles and dp()/style metrics when extending the interface. Stable widget IDs and per-view state preserve selection and edits. CyUI integrates through add_subdirectory or FetchContent; it has no installed find_package(CyUI) package.

2. Editor tools

Assets supplies folder trees, grid/list presentation, thumbnail callbacks, search and drag/drop requests. Inspector supplies typed properties, collapsible groups, exact integers, validation and draft editing. Commands returns action IDs from a searchable palette; Diagnostics presents bounded logs and navigable messages.

Keep edits transactional

Editors return proposals with begin, update, commit and cancel phases. Keep original model values during a gesture, validate a committed proposal and record it as one host Undo transaction. Increment the supplied revision when host data changes.

The host owns asset storage, imports, file operations, selection models, preview generation, validation and Undo. CyUI does not load or save application projects.

3. Graphs, audio & data

Canvas is the common grid/pan/zoom layer. Nodes adds cards, pins and connection requests; Plots adds linear/log series, histograms and heatmaps; Curves adds editable keyframes and handles; Timeline adds lanes and clips. AudioViews uses prepared waveform envelopes and sampled spectra/scopes. Audio supplies knobs, faders and peak/RMS meters.

The host supplies graph types, compatibility, validation, processing, interpolation, snapping policy, time units, transport and data reduction. No audio engine, decoder, FFT or shader compiler is linked by these presentation modules.

Prepare and cache models when source data changes. Supply visible or bounded data to each view; consult the module guide for limits, reduction helpers and edit contracts.

4. Code & comparison

Code owns the shared syntax catalogue, source annotations and extensible language registry. CodeEditor adds the bundled native TextEditor backend with Undo/Redo and advanced editor hooks. Diff displays unified or split prepared text comparisons and provides hunk navigation.

Use codeLanguages() and codeLanguageForPath() instead of duplicating a language list in the host. Register declarative rules or a host lexer callback for extensions. Register and unregister outside concurrent rendering; retain callbacks until views no longer use them.

Git access, history queries, merge actions, language servers, compilation and debugging remain host responsibilities. Python’s editor is a separate multiline editor with a syntax preview; it does not expose all native C++ TextEditor features.

5. Images & documents

Images navigates host textures and presents checkerboard, crop and gradient-stop interactions. Viewport wraps a host-rendered surface with an orbit-camera model and transform controls. DocumentViews presents a Markdown subset, tables, code blocks, links and transcripts.

The host owns textures and their lifetime, image/video decoding, rendering, file links, conversation state and remote services. Use Web for a real browser; DocumentViews is not a browser or a full HTML renderer.

6. Filtering & languages

Core includes optional TextFilter/filterBox controls for panels and a filterMenu for nested action trees. Each view retains its own query. Matching searches English and translated captions, uses all query words and folds Latin accents. Inspector can accept a shared filter without acquiring another optional dependency.

English is the default language and French is built in. Use tr() for text and trLabel() for interactive labels, so switching languages preserves widget identities. Add application messages and extra languages with registerTranslations().

C++
cyui::setLocale("fr");
cyui::registerTranslations("fr", {{"app.export", "Exporter"}});
if (cyui::button(cyui::trLabel("app.export", "Export").c_str())) {
    exportDocument();
}

The built-in catalogue translates CyUI controls, not user documents, filenames, source code or arbitrary host labels. Supply appropriate fonts and fallback glyphs. RTL layout, complex shaping, plural rules and locale-specific date/number formatting require host work.

7. Python

From a local CyUI checkout, install the package. imgui-bundle is a UI dependency; optional data models can be imported without creating a renderer. Python requires version 3.10 or newer.

Shell
python -m pip install -e .
Python
import cyui as c
from cyui_modules import plots, inspector

c.set_locale("fr")
# Draw inside your application's ImGui frame.
if c.primary_button(c.tr_label("Save")):
    save_document()

Choose optional families explicitly from cyui_modules. Follow examples/python_modules.py for the real gallery and initialize the host’s ImGui frame/backend normally. Native CodeEditor-specific features are not all mirrored by the Python editor.

8. Web / CEF

Web supplies the browser surface contract, input forwarding, origin policy, versioned messages and theme/localization bridge. WebCEF is an opt-in off-screen Chromium Embedded Framework adapter that paints into a host-owned texture. Compile TypeScript to JavaScript with the web application’s own build.

Supply the exact CEF SDK/runtime for each OS and architecture. The host owns initialization, subprocesses, sandbox policy, runtime packaging, message authorization and texture lifetime. CEF is neither downloaded nor enabled by selecting all ordinary modules.

The portable Windows demo includes a Web preview, not a working browser runtime. The repository records native/Python CEF round-trip testing on Windows. Linux/macOS adapter packaging has not been locally validated.

9. Unreal Editor

The optional connector embeds CyUI in native Slate editor panels. It owns ImGui contexts, input, clipboard, font textures and the Slate renderer. The consuming plugin owns its windows, menus and tool state; merely loading the module creates no tools.

Shell
python tools/package_unreal.py --layout module --output build/unreal-module/CyUI --modules Core Plots Inspector

Copy the prepared CyUI directory into your plugin’s Source directory and declare the Editor module and its Build.cs dependency. Several consumers should share one provider, or use uniquely named embedded copies. Read the detailed guide before choosing the layout.

This is an Editor-only C++ integration. It is not a UMG, Blueprint or gameplay runtime backend. Unreal Engine is supplied and licensed separately. Local validation was performed on Windows.

CyUI’s own code, documentation and adapters use MIT. Preserve its notice and all notices for distributed dependencies, including Dear ImGui, stb, TextEditor and the selected syntax engines/data. CEF/Chromium and Unreal Engine retain their separate licenses and distribution requirements.

The versioned demo is 1.2.0. The repository does not declare an alpha/beta designation and development is active. Validate each selected component and platform before shipping your application.
